item.title: [Message Center] MC1546447 Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Updated recipient inclusion logic for threat protection policies
item.description:
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 will change recipient inclusion logic in threat protection policies from Match all (AND) to Match any (OR) when multiple recipient types are specified. This update, rolling out in December 2026, expands policy scope upon modification but does not auto-convert existing policies.

Microsoft Defender XDR · stayInformed

item.title: [New] Defender for Office 365 threat policies switch multi-condition recipient targeting from AND to OR; an existing policy converts when an admin next edits it, and its scope can widen
item.description:
A policy written as 'users in group X AND in domain Y' becomes 'X OR Y' on its next edit, so an anti-phishing, Safe Links or Safe Attachments policy meant for a narrow population can silently start applying to a whole domain, and a stricter policy can override the one the SOC expects for those mailboxes.

Defender XDR · Before December, export the recipient conditions of every threat policy (Get-AntiPhishRule, Get-SafeLinksRule, Get-SafeAttachmentRule, Get-HostedContentFilterRule) and flag those that combine two condition types; review each one's OR scope before anyone edits it.

item.title: [Due in 5 days] App Governance permissions change for three Entra roles as Defender XDR Unified RBAC takes over
item.description:
Two compliance roles silently lose an app-governance capability and one security role gains it: an app-governance policy nobody can edit, or one an unexpected role can now edit, is a control gap either way.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-11-15 · Before mid-November, list who reaches App Governance through Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator or Cloud App Security Administrator, review custom Defender XDR Unified RBAC roles for Defender for Cloud Apps, and reassign affected people to a supported Entra role or a custom Unified RBAC role on least privilege.

item.title: [New] Microsoft Threat Intelligence: fake-download campaign drops proxyware, BOINC miners and adware from trojanized Inno Setup installers
item.description:
Proxyware turns a managed endpoint into an exit node for other people's traffic, so a SYSTEM scheduled task from a 'free' installer is an attribution and data-exposure problem, not just adware.

Threat Intel · Run the post's advanced hunting queries for the offer_execution callback and Inno temp-directory execution, audit SYSTEM scheduled tasks for WorldProxyPool, and confirm cloud-delivered protection, tamper protection and the relevant ASR rules are on.

item.title: [New] Defender RBAC is switched on automatically for Defender and Sentinel portal experiences, about 30 days after an in-portal notice, from early December 2026
item.description:
After activation, Defender and Sentinel portal access is decided by imported Defender RBAC roles, not by the legacy workload roles a SOC audited; an import that maps an analyst too broadly or too narrowly changes incident and email access without any new grant being made.

Defender XDR · When the banner appears, review every imported role and scope under Permissions > Roles in the Defender portal, test an analyst and a Security Reader account against email, device and Sentinel views, move any role automation to the Defender RBAC Graph API, and update runbooks before 2 December 2026.

item.description:

item.title: [New] Defender URBAC permission 'Emails associated with alerts' now also gates preview and download of emails behind the two malicious-URL-click alerts
item.description:
Analysts triaging URL-click alerts lose or gain access to the underlying email depending on one URBAC permission, so a role that lacks it slows every click investigation.

Defender XDR · Check which Defender URBAC custom roles carry 'Emails associated with alerts' and grant it to the analysts who triage URL-click alerts; keep it off roles that should not read mail content.
